topics.chapterTitle: Evolving Modular Applications into Independent Services
topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: A team notices that several components are difficult to change together and proposes making each one a service. The proposal may create independent deployment, but it may also turn every former function call into a synchronous network dependency. The result can be a distributed monolith: separate processes that still require coordinated releases and fail together.

topics.title: 2.1.1 Separating Domain Decisions from Transport and Storage
topics.summary: The domain layer decides whether work is valid and how a valid request is interpreted. A transport adapter turns bytes into a request and turns a result into bytes. A storage adapter maintains records according to persistence and concurrency rules. Mixing these responsibilities makes a change in one mechanism leak into every test.

topics.title: 2.1.2 Grouping Changes That Belong Together
topics.summary: Cohesion is about the relationship among responsibilities, not file size alone. Validation of a job’s input and its canonical representation often belong together because changing one affects the other’s correctness. A terminal formatter and a durable transaction usually do not belong together merely because both are short functions.

blocks.text: Ask what changes together during a feature. If adding a new job state always requires edits to five services, the boundary may have split one invariant across too many owners. If changing a metrics backend forces a change to the request domain, an implementation dependency may have become part of the public contract unnecessarily.

blocks.text: A useful module exports a small set of operations and hides details that callers do not need to coordinate. Its tests should describe those operations, not inspect private data structures. A test that reaches into a private queue layout can make a harmless implementation change appear to violate a public contract.

The important question is where independent invariants and independent change ownership already exist, rather than how many lines a style rule permits.

topics.chapterTitle: Evolving Modular Applications into Independent Services
topics.title: 2.2.1 Understanding the Modular Monolith
topics.summary: A modular monolith is one deployment unit with meaningful internal boundaries. It can contain separate domain libraries, transport adapters, persistence components, and tests without requiring those components to communicate over the network. Calls can use ordinary values and exceptions under one process’s lifetime model.

cards.question: Explain Understanding the Modular Monolith in your own words.
cards.answer: A modular monolith is one deployment unit with meaningful internal boundaries. It can contain separate domain libraries, transport adapters, persistence components, and tests without requiring those components to communicate over the network. Calls can use ordinary values and exceptions under one process’s lifetime model.

blocks.text: The main advantage for early design is reversibility. A module boundary can be adjusted while a function call remains local. Once many independently deployed clients depend on a wire protocol, changing it requires compatibility across a rollout window. Starting locally can therefore reduce the cost of discovering the right abstraction.
rich: The main advantage for early design is reversibility. A module boundary can be adjusted while a function call remains local. Once many independently deployed clients depend on a wire protocol, changing it requires compatibility across a rollout window. Starting locally can therefore reduce the cost of discovering the right abstraction.

blocks.text: The design still needs discipline. Global mutable state, shared implementation headers, and unrestricted access to every table can erase the boundaries despite a neat directory tree. CMake targets can make include visibility and dependencies explicit, but they cannot by themselves enforce semantic ownership of data. Reviews and tests must check both.

CMake targets can make include visibility and dependencies explicit, but they cannot by themselves enforce semantic ownership of data. Reviews and tests must check both.

blocks.text: A single process is not automatically a single failure concern. Different thread pools, queues, and resource budgets can provide partial isolation within it. Conversely, several containers on the same overloaded host can share a failure domain. Treat deployment as a concrete resource arrangement, not an architectural virtue assigned by name.

topics.title: 2.2.2 Establishing When a Remote Boundary Is Justified
topics.summary: A remote boundary becomes useful when its benefit outweighs the new coordination cost. An expensive worker may need a different hardware pool. A sensitive data owner may need a separate access boundary. Two teams may require independent release schedules. A service may need to continue accepting durable intent while a downstream worker is restarted.

blocks.text: Remote boundaries also constrain interfaces. A pointer cannot be transferred as a meaningful cross-process object identity. A reference to a caller’s vector cannot remain valid on another host. Errors can occur after the remote operation has committed, and the caller may not know which outcome occurred. These differences should be visible in the API rather than hidden behind a stub that suggests ordinary local-call semantics.

The extraction is safer when the network is the last new mechanism rather than the first method used to discover the contract.

topics.chapterTitle: Evolving Modular Applications into Independent Services
topics.title: 2.3.1 Avoiding Shared-Database Service Boundaries
topics.summary: Two services that write each other’s tables are often coupled more tightly than their network diagram suggests. A schema change by one owner can break another’s queries. A transaction from either process can hold locks needed by the other. A repair script can bypass domain validation that only exists in one service’s code.

blocks.text: For HarborDispatch, the gateway and worker have separate database files. The gateway sends a command; it does not insert a receipt directly into the worker’s table. This intentionally creates an acknowledgment gap that the protocol must handle. Shared access might appear simpler, but it would teach the wrong authority model for independent services.

This intentionally creates an acknowledgment gap that the protocol must handle. Shared access might appear simpler, but it would teach the wrong authority model for independent services.

blocks.text: Sometimes a shared database is a deliberate transitional design. Document it as such. Identify table ownership, permitted readers and writers, migration coordination, and the conditions for removing the shared dependency. Pretending the database is private while several services bypass the owner is worse than acknowledging the coupling honestly.

An exported event, snapshot, or reporting view can create an explicit contract instead. That contract has freshness and recovery costs of its own, which later chapters examine.

Pretending the database is private while several services bypass the owner is worse than acknowledging the coupling honestly.

Reporting queries deserve particular attention. A read-only join across tables may still lock in another service’s internal schema. An exported event, snapshot, or reporting view can create an explicit contract instead. That contract has freshness and recovery costs of its own, which later chapters examine.

blocks.text: The design has paid for remote communication without gaining independent responsibility. To repair it, identify the invariant boundary. Validation and durable acceptance can remain together. Computation can be asynchronous after acceptance. Status formatting can operate from the stored state without participating in the acceptance transaction. Independent release follows from a versioned contract and separately owned data, not from assigning a port number to each function.

blocks.text: A shared C++ “common” library can recreate the same coupling. When every service consumes its newest headers and changes together, the library is effectively a global release boundary. Prefer stable, narrow schemas and explicit compatibility windows. Share mechanisms where appropriate, but do not use a shared build as a substitute for a protocol contract.

blocks.text: The interface is not actually a service contract. The row handle belongs to one database session, the pointer belongs to one address space, and the vector’s in-memory layout belongs to one implementation. The extraction must instead define durable input values: operation version, key, bounded integer, and any required domain options.

blocks.text: The next question is failure ownership. In the monolith, a thrown exception might unwind one call stack. Across the process boundary, the caller can time out while the callee continues. The adapter needs a transport result and a domain result, and the application needs a decision for uncertain completion. Those requirements are architectural changes introduced by extraction, not accidental complexity to hide in a helper function.

blocks.text: Draw the dependency direction before writing the network adapter. Domain validation should remain usable without opening a socket. The store should not depend on terminal formatting. The adapter should translate wire values into the same domain request that local tests use. This allows the monolithic path and the service path to be compared against the same semantics during migration.

For pure computations, shadow execution can compare results without changing authoritative state. For mutations, shadowing must not perform a second external effect. A safe shadow path may validate or simulate rather than execute.

A benchmark of the computation alone cannot justify extraction for latency. Other benefits, such as independent deployment or isolation, may still justify it, but they should be named honestly.

A fallback is useful only if it preserves the same authority and result contract. Starting both mutation paths independently is not a safe fallback simply because one is local.
